title: Prague Castle founded
summary: A fortified seat arose at Prague Castle around 880 and became the enduring center of Bohemian power.

title: Vysehrad becomes a royal seat
summary: Vratislaus II established Vysehrad as a principal royal residence in the later 11th century.

title: St Vitus Cathedral begun
summary: Construction of the present Gothic cathedral at Prague Castle began in 1344 after Prague became an archbishopric.

title: Charles University founded
summary: Charles IV founded Charles University in 1348, creating the first university in Central Europe north of the Alps.

title: New Town founded
locationNote: The foundation reshaped the wider New Town district; this marker sits in Charles Square as its central civic space.
summary: Charles IV founded Prague's New Town in 1348 as a vast planned urban extension beyond the Old Town walls.

title: Charles Bridge begun
summary: Construction of Charles Bridge began in 1357 to replace the flood-damaged Judith Bridge across the Vltava.

title: First Defenestration of Prague
summary: A crowd led by Jan Zelivsky threw town officials from the New Town Hall windows in 1419, helping ignite the Hussite Wars.

title: Battle of Vitkov Hill
locationNote: The fighting ranged across the ridge above Prague; this marker is placed near the modern Vitkov summit.
summary: Hussite forces under Jan Zizka repelled a crusader assault on Vitkov Hill in July 1420.

title: Rudolf II moves his court to Prague
summary: Rudolf II transferred his imperial court to Prague in 1583 and made the city a major political and cultural center.

title: Rabbi Loew and the Golem tradition
summary: Rabbi Judah Loew was a leading Prague scholar in the late 16th century and later folklore tied him to the city's Golem legend.

title: Brahe and Kepler in Prague
locationNote: Tycho Brahe and Johannes Kepler worked at several Prague sites; this marker is a compromise location in the historic center.
summary: Tycho Brahe and Johannes Kepler worked in Prague around 1600, where Kepler later used Brahe's observations to derive planetary laws.

title: Second Defenestration of Prague
summary: Bohemian nobles hurled imperial governors from a Prague Castle window in 1618, triggering the Bohemian Revolt.

title: Battle of White Mountain
locationNote: The battle spread across fields west of the city; this marker is placed near the White Mountain memorial area.
summary: Imperial and Catholic League forces defeated the Bohemian revolt at White Mountain in 1620.

title: Execution of 27 Bohemian lords
summary: Habsburg authorities executed 27 leaders of the Bohemian revolt in Old Town Square on 21 June 1621.

title: National Theatre opens
summary: The National Theatre first opened in 1881 as a major symbol of Czech cultural and political self-assertion.

title: Josefov clearance
locationNote: The redevelopment affected much of the former Jewish Quarter; this marker is placed near its historic core.
summary: Large parts of Prague's historic Jewish Quarter were demolished and rebuilt between 1893 and 1913 in a sweeping urban clearance.

title: Czechoslovakia declared
summary: The Czechoslovak declaration of independence was proclaimed in Prague on 28 October 1918 as Habsburg rule collapsed.

title: Nazi occupation begins
summary: German troops occupied Prague in March 1939 and Prague Castle became the seat of the new Protectorate regime.

title: Heydrich assassination
summary: Czechoslovak resistance fighters attacked Reinhard Heydrich at a bend in Liben in May 1942, prompting brutal Nazi reprisals.

title: Prague Spring invasion
summary: Warsaw Pact forces invaded Czechoslovakia in August 1968, and fighting around the radio building became one of Prague's defining scenes.

title: Jan Palach self-immolation
summary: Student Jan Palach set himself on fire in Wenceslas Square in January 1969 to protest the post-invasion suppression of reform.

title: Velvet Revolution
summary: The police assault on a student march at Narodni trida on 17 November 1989 helped trigger the Velvet Revolution.

title: Vltava floods
locationNote: The flooding affected multiple districts along the river; this marker sits near the Karlin waterfront.
summary: The 2002 floods inundated major parts of Prague, including Karlin and long stretches of the Vltava embankment.
